I don't think this game is for me but I can certainly see it's appeal. Rust is a pure PvP game - You are dropped onto an island with nothing but a rock and are expected to move up a tech ladder until you can really take care of yourself. The issue, which is pointed out a number of times in the "not recommend" reviews, is that you have to be ready and willing to put A LOT of time into your first session. You have to not only live long enough (everyone is trying to kill you) to gather a large amount of items (everyone wants to take your stuff) to build a base but also secure that base (everyone want to wreck your base). Anything less will certainly result in the loss of not only your character but all of your progress as well. For some I am sure it is fun but for me the barrier to entry is far to tedious. If you really enjoy this game I would suggest going into research science or telemarketing. Edit - I found out that you can make your own server. Afte playing for a bit without being killed every five minutes, this is atually a pretty good game. It is clearly made to PvP but it is also fun to explore. It's a shame the focus of this game is getting in it's own way.

In this game, you play as an Immigration Control Officer of a fictional dystopian country. This means you will be doing tedious stuff like ensuring that the passport and other documents have not expired, that a potential immigrant's work permit passport number matches with his presented passport, that the picture on the passport actually matches the person and other trivialities. You do not have the luxury to peruse the papers at your leisure because you have a limited amount of time each day to process immigrants - your daily pay is based on how many people you accurately serve. If you want to be good at this game, it will demand that you memorize the *geography* of this fictional world, like which cities belong in the country of Republia, and which districts are in your home country of Arstotzkan. So if you enjoy filling your head with completely useless trivia, then go for it! I'd personally spend that time learning real world geography if my inclinations ever took me in that direction (although for censorship/political reasons, the game creators wisely refrained from adding any Real World countries). The game is a monotonous drone of menial work. Playing it felt like work to me. Story mode offers occasional flashes of excitement when you are asked to perform some "cloak & dagger" operations or resolve some moral dillemma, but this happens around 10% of the game and is not enough reward to chore the rest. The developers could have chosen to add a lot more "custom events" to make the game more engaging, but I guess it was not done due to time/budget constraints, laziness, or possibly a desire to achieve realism. I guess a border official's life is pretty boring - in game you meet a former border official and he tells you something to the tune of "I'm glad I'm no longer in that business". In a nutshell: This game is work. If you want work that badly, then go get a job instead of playing this game.

100% "Kingdom Come: Deliverance" is a first-person RPG in the vein of Elder Scrolls, with a lot of familiar ideas and designs. Now while "Kingdom Come" has been called a sandbox and flaunts itself as the ultimate open world, it is unfortunately not that open. It is about as open as an Elder Scrolls adventure like Skyrim, and really, truly not much more. The way "Kingdom Come" sells itself at first makes you think about all kinds of possibilities, but shortly thereafter you realize there's usually 1 or 2 ways to go about most things. Liberate a poor horse from a bandit camp. Sell it? Buy a saddle and keep it as your own? Set it free to roam in a friendly part of the wilds? Nope. Impossible. It will go back to the bandit camp the moment you wander too far, or you can arrow it to the head and lug around exhausting amounts of meat to sell. The world feels small more often than not. What makes "Kingdom Come" truly different is that it forces us to build our character from the absolute ground up (we cannot swim or even read, to start) and tells a story based in the real world, where magic and monsters are nowhere to be found except in the hearts of men. Combat is scary because it takes time and genuine care to learn, and it is difficult. A lot of the game is difficult. Picking locks is horrendous at first, until you get the hang of the mechanics. Nothing here is easy. Even going on a long journey and realising you are tired or hungry is delightfully challenging as you scavenge food with relief from an empty camp site found along your path. But this is the game's charm. Things we often take for granted, like the daily tasks of living, become important here like we have rarely seen before. What ultimately makes this game stand out for me are the absolutely gorgeous and epic, powerful cinematics that drive and underlie the simple, heartfelt story. I highly recommend "Kingdom Come: Deliverance" because it reminds me of the fun I've had with Elder Scrolls but provides a very welcome start-over for our adventure-loving hearts. I would absolutely jump all over any sequel, with fingers crossed that it might give us that sandbox we longed for originally.

Four wooden planks can in turn make a crafting table (place 4 wooden planks in a 2x2 square) and place the crafting table to use it. Right click your crafting table to access it, this crafting grid is a 3x3 square, big enough for all of the craftable items in Minecraft. The first tools the player should craft are a wooden pickaxe and a wooden sword. If any stone blocks are exposed close by, the player can mine them with a wooden pickaxe for 19 blocks of cobblestone. This is the amount the player needs to create every basic tool they'll need for this tutorial: a sword, a pickaxe (you'll need the upgraded pickaxe for iron and other blocks), an axe, a shovel, a hoe, and a furnace. You'll need the furnace to cook meat for food and smelt any ore you mine with your pickaxe. Once the player has a stone axe, they should try to get more wood as time allows; extra wood is useful in many ways, from securing and equipping your base to making charcoal, or simply crafting into planks for quadruple the number of building blocks.

EDIT: Changing the recommendation to a thumbs-down after the constant torrent of pathetically inept patches. It seems like they release a MANY-GB patch every month to promote for-fee features I'm not interested in and each patch introduces new game-breaking bugs. Then, there's a series of patches to fix what their inept developers broke. It's too much hassle even to keep the game installed for an occasional romp. This game is pretty decent but also pretty far from great. The campaign is a mess - nearly every mission requires focusing on one particular type of animal in one particular area, but a shocking number of such missions request animals that simply don't spawn in the target areas. For a while, the developer actively tried to correct the situation with patches, but since the update that added jackrabbits shuffled spawn zones around they seem to have simply abandoned the game. It's a bizarre situation where it seems the developer is satisfied pushing broken content, but it's not the only one. Plenty of other features, like the all terrain vehicles, tents, and portable blinds have a rough, unfinished feel that probably detract more from the game than they add. It's unfortunate. The biggest disappointment about this game is the failure to provide a tweakable sandbox. I'd like to see sliders or console options to adjust game population, modify time cycles, spawn props and all manner of other stuff. The game also desperately needs mod support, allowing players to add new weapon types, ammunition types, game modes, etc. The game could ideally be a realistic hunting simulator one minute and a Duck Dynasty/Demolition Ranch simulator the next. I'm guessing Expansive believes they stand to make big money by drip-feeding content and features, but making a truly great sandbox game with broad appeal would be a better bet.

You can build almost anything you wish, indulge your creativity, or just build huge mines, max out on money and buy your way through the game. There are a multitude of issues with this game from balance issue on both survivor and killer side, such as crutch mechanics, broken killer abilities and addons. Same with perks on both sides. Some are not expressly broken but are completely unfun to deal with. This game also has massive issues with hitboxes and server connections. The combination of the two will have you getting hit from china by the killer when you play survivor and missing grabs and hits as killer when playing against survivors. The community... The community for the most part is toxic af and myself am guilty of this. A lot of the toxicity in this game stems from the broken/unbalanced/straight up unfun aspects of this game. Other issues with this game include, poor optimization and ui design. The game does not run very well for a game that is not that graphically intense and from 2016 using the Unreal engine. Menus can be clunky and sometimes broken leading you to be kicked from your lobby just because you activate a challenge within the game. As I post this it's Dec. 15, 2019 and until about two months ago I could not run this game without massive stuttering issues unless I used a Nvidia driver that was almost a year old. I spent a lot of time looking into the issue and the best I could find from a rep from Behavior was that "it's windows 10's fault" But then about two months ago they updated their engine and now my issues is resolved... I still have an issues with crashes if I use the most recent drivers and try to play this game. My gpu is a 970, so if you have a 900 series card be cautious. Oh, bugs. Lots and lots of bugs. Every month and a half and two months the have a mid chapter update and a chapter update, and I can not recall an update where they did not break some aspect of the game. Some of the greatest hits include being hit through solid objects, broken sound, falling through the map, being put in a certain part of the map and losing control of your character, getting a black of grey screen, randomly losing the ability use your keyboard in game (could still use it in google and other applications and in the game only after the match had ended), and others I can not recall. Another thing I have a personal issues with is, the devs seem more interested in releasing cosmetics in their ingame shop than actually fixing the game. (If you like cosmetics, this game's got em in spades) The game 'can' be great fun if played with friends. Though played solo it can also be fun but I would not hedge you bets on that. At the end of the day, it's your money. If you want to try it out, go for it. Update Most recent update 9/8/20 they broke more things. With the graphics update to gens, pallets and a two maps, has come massive performance issues. These issues existed on the beta version of the update and they still pushed it live. PS4 and Xbox players are experiencing it as well. These developers are very bad at keeping the game in a healthy state. My recommendation remains unchanged.

I'm a bit sleepy but not yet sleepy-sleepy. Might as well write a review and help people out. ++++ (PROS) -Really fun base game. If I were to describe the gameplay, I'd say it's a bit like Company of Heroes but without the cover and with powerful hero units of course. AND yes, the MOBA-like objectives. Unit micro is the name of the game here and tactics is still a big part especially in the early and mid game. See, the game has these things called Escalation Phases where the resource income per generator, percent refunded after unit death, turret damage, shield generator health, etc. This means that early game where income is low and refund rate is high, there's a focus on aggressive skirmishes. This slowly evolves into massive army clashes in the late game, the things you see in the gameplay trailers. Escalation Phases increase every 10 minutes. -I like the evolving nature of the tactics you need. So it starts with small units skirmishes right? Then you evolve into medium scale armies where your composition comes into play. You start thinking about counters and stuff. Then it evolves into this massive clash of armies and then you're now thinking large scale. How do you break him? Where do you push? Do you have enough for a multi-pronged attack? Stuff like that. -Refunds. Yeah, so ever think about RTS and how you're dead when you lose the first engagement so you'd rather turtle up? Well in DoW III, units get refunds for the first few minutes so go ahead and lose your units, as long as you can rebuild, you can come back. Worry free! Also, I don't know if it's because of refunds but I'm putting it here too. We all know late game there's no shortage of army wiping abilities and heroes right? Believe it or not, losing your army is not the end of the world. If you are on top of your macro-management, there is enough of a breather for you to produce another army that could stand a chance against what's left of your opponents. I think this might be because of the objective system -No rushes. The objectives means that the equivalent of rushes and cheese is basically gone. This could be a pro or a con. I'm taking this as a pro since I often play DoW III after an exhausting ladder session of Starcraft II and the break from cheese is welcome. This doesn't mean you can't take down map objectives. Remember the Escalation Phases? Objective health also scale with the Phases so a ragtag group of units can still take down a Turret objective provided that you have created an opening while your opponent rebuilds after a wipe. -Hero micro. This again could be a pro or a con. I find it really fun to micro hero units. It reminds me a bit of Warcraft III. Line units are important in DoW III but not as important as heroes. No, it's not a MOBA, shut up. It's more of an RTS game than friggin' DOW II! You don't level your heroes in-game (there's a progression system out of the game where you earn stuff like Doctrines and skins). They're just there to micro. They die quickly if you have the appropriate counter but they are also VERY POWERFUL. Probably going to put this into the cons. -Pretty meh to slightly passable campaign. The story serves to move the game forward. It's serviceable, nothing to write home about. Missions are decent but the pacing could work. It alternates between the three races and you never play the same race twice. It works in a narrative sense but sometimes you just want to play more SM or Ork or Eldar in a row, you know? ---- (CONS) - LACK OF POLISH. Game bugging out sometimes where there's this loud ringing sounds which I have to restart the game to fix. I had units teleport and vanish into the warp in the single player. The UI is sluggish and slow to respond. WHY IS THERE NO CONCEDE BUTTON, RELIC? Remember the out-of-game progression system for Elites I was talking about? Turns out you don't get EXP if you quit a match. So if you're stuck with a really toxic team-mate or the game turns against you so much that there's literally no chance of a comeback, you have to literally wait for your opponent to finish it. Really? -Powerful elites. NO THIS IS NOT A MOBA SHUT UP. But still, I really hate this. I wanted elites to be powerful support units. Remember Warcraft III and how they did heroes? I guess they had to balance heroes out to be consistent through the Escalation Phases or something so they have this constant power level throughout the game. This means Nuker heroes can wipe your units in the early game since they need to be able to wipe units in the late game too (because there's going to be much much more units in the late game). This is so frustrating for me. You could be winning an engagement in the early game but a sudden spell from out of nowhere will take out half of your squads. So RIP, fall back and recoup (at least there's refunds). That window of opening is gone thanks to one spell. Hurr Durr. -The massive army clashes could be a pain if you're playing 3v3. This may be a little of a L2P issue, but I'm having problems seeing what's happening in the late game. -FEATURE and CONTENT STARVED. I get having one mode for multi but 8 maps???? No co-op too. Sucks. DO I RECOMMEND IT? That depends on what's important to you. I bought it full price because I find the base game really, really fun despite some frustrations. And because it's WH40k Kappa. I got 15 hours of entertainment already and that number will just be rising since I still enjoy the multiplayer. That's worth $60 to me. But if you're not really a fan of 40k, or put off by the lack of content, I recommend waiting for a sale and/or waiting for more content (if Relic will do free content updates, that is). Objectively, this is a $40 game at its current condition and I recommend waiting for it now. I am hitting RECOMMEND though because I believe that Relic has something with DoW III that they could build upon if they play their cards right. I bet that a large part of you on the fence people or people currently hating the game based on videos and articles without playing it would probably love it if you give it a chance. Yes it's different from DoW I and DoW II. Just like how DoW II was different from DoW I. It's NOT a downgrade. It's more of a side grade. All three games are sidegrades tbh. That's just how DoW is. They aren't sequels in the strictests sense. They're more of like different games sharing the same leitmotiff. I hope I helped you if you're on the fence with this game. This game is amazing. It took me a few playthroughs and even a few months to realize just how well this game has been developed and what it has become. What took me by suprise was how well the world felt. It was so alive with birds flying everywere, a plethora of wildlife to hunt, various things to explore and look at, like effegies / abandoned camps/ caves/ breath taking scenery, and ofcourse the mutants that run rampant throughtout. Not only are the visuals on par, but the sound effects are hyper realistic too! Chopping a tree and hearing the wood splintering and branches bending before it thuds onto the earth. The wildlife I mentioned above creates an amazing ambience that serves only to immerse you more. Night time as well in some areas away from the windy beach will provide you with creepy and unknown noises. Aside from the 10/10 visuals and audio the game continues to serve customers by providing a solid combat system. While the enemy variations arent numerous, there are still enough to keep you on your toes until you have become familiar with all the tactics required to fight each mob type. Multiplayer combat can get a little wonky at times with suddend framrate freezes lasting about half a second but nothing bad enough to get you killed. None the less there exists a healthy number of weapons to dispatch all those pesky mutants! Crafting is a solid aspect of the game too. You can create some pretty nifty buildings or fortresses to gaurd against enemies who seek to destoy your safe haven. You dont really have to farm too many materials to create a sweet base aside from chopping down 1 million trees but there are methods in place to assist speeding it up. Sadly there is no 'snap to fit' option which makes building a little annoying at times but no serious reason to hold it against the game. Finally the story. For new players its a wonder! you find clues all over the island in the form of torn pages, pictures, and other mediums of mystery that together begin to make a little sense towards the end while still leaving a few questions unanswered. Once you get the keycard and reach the final door. wow.......What an amzing ending to a sweet game. After beating the game for my first time I saw everything in a new light when starting a new game. Full price or on sale doesnt matter, this game is worth every penny and more. I heavily suggest buying this title and in my opinion is best enjoyed with 1 other friend for some sweet horror coop fun. With the release of the Emperor Edition, which included the free campaign pack "Imperator Augustus", Rome II is a much improved beast from the dark days of it's launch. - General battle speeds have been reduced, allowing more time for the player to either attempt tactical maneuvre or simply enjoy the spectacle. - Performance has been significantly improved across the board. The AI, in campaign and battle, has had many bugs ironed out. - Of particular note are siege battles, where there is now a legitimate challenge. - On the campaign gameplay, the building and politics systems were extensively overhauled, although politics does still suffer from a certain level of unresponsiveness and inexplicable behaviour. This is still a different experience from previous titles, but one thoroughly worth giving a shot. If you're still on the fence then there are Let's Plays aplenty on Youtube. ****Original Review**** Graphically impressive. Excellent combat animations and sound effects. Streamlined empire management. That's the good stuff. The campaign itself has the depth of a puddle. The much vaunted politics system is pathetic. Diplomacy and CAI in general is broken. Essentially, you'll be doing exactly the same thing 250 turns in as you were 20 turns in. Battles are ridiculously fast. Units are horribly balanced. Plenty of features and controls are broken or poorly redesigned. Voice work is mostly poor. 90% of battles are sieges and siege battles are currently broken. All in all, an extremely poor addition to the Total War series that suffers as much from bad design choices as it does from a lack of optimization and extensive technical issues.

Which in turn make the AI capable of doing ridiculous things when they're low on provinces and should be crippled. The thing is one province AI cna at times field more units then a small player empire. Totally unbalancing the game and really jarring with the now limited armies for the player. Lastly let me mention the DLCs. It started with a pre-order DLC that included some of the most popular nations to play as. That was later sold for a meagre €7,50... This was followed by a DLC that was free for early adapters that added units to the meagre roster of the northern steppe people. Decent DLC, decent move but once again cost about €7,50 now. Let's not forget the Blood and Gore DLC. Addign cool visual effects. It was sold seperately to avoid a high rating for the game, I get that but for some reason it costs several euro's and never goes on sale. Last but not least lets give the barbarian factions that have the least amount of units some new ones but only if you buy a mini campaign that cost €15,- I don't want to buy a mini campaign I'll never play just to enhance my favorite factions. Overal a shitty chapter in the history of Total War. Let's hope not the last but I'm not looking forward to the next with such boundless joy as I used to.

Have been playing this game sense legacy so I have gotten to experience almost all aspects of this game. First off I am not sure why there is so many negative reviews for this game and would have to assume they mostly are from people who are tired of dying a lot. So im going to break my review into pros and cons and hopefully you will be able to decide if this is the type of game for you. Pros • Building – You can build buildings with almost no limitation. As long as the ground is level enough you can build on it. If you want to build a 30 story tall building you can. If you want to build a castle you can. If you want to build a house on the water so you can get the best views of the morning sun rise you can. • Crafting – This game has a huge crafting system. Pretty much anything in the game you use you are going to have to craft it from either wood, stone, metal, cloth or one of the many other resources. You can craft anything from a wooden spear to an assault rifle • Blueprints – When you start the game you have a limited amount of items you can craft but as you travel around the map you will be able to find blueprints for better items that will be able to make your life in rust easier. • Raiding – Though it sucks when it happens to you it’s a lot of fun to do to others. Almost any player built thing can be destroyed so it can be a lot of fun traveling with your friends breaking into other player’s buildings and looting their valuables. • Updates – unlike most Alpha games I have seen being sold on Steam the developers actually care about their game. They do weekly updates and most the time it is some pretty big changes. Bringing in new items or improving how existing things work. They are also very on top of bugs. Normally having them fixed within a day or two. You are able to check the official site to see what updates they are working on for the following week so it’s nice to know what to be prepared for. • Graphics – They have put a lot of time into making this game look beautiful. Everything from how the grass looks to getting the reflection of the moon on the water just right. You will spend a lot of time just enjoying the view in this game. Cons • Community – Sadly the biggest problem with this game is the community for every one nice person you find you are going to get at least 20 people who will kill you for the rock in your hand. I would highly recommend that if you see another person in game that you don’t know you just turn and run because they can and probably will kill you. • Dying – You are going to die a lot in this game. Pretty much every time you log on to this game expect that you will wake up with nothing. Even when you log out your body stays in game so people can still kill you and loot your stuff. It can be a lot of fun trying to figure out ways to keep yourself safe but it can be pretty annoying if you just worked on something for 10 hours to log on the next day and find that it’s all gone. • Lag – Currently there is a pretty bad issue with lag in the game depending on where you are. The areas with a lot of player made stuff can get pretty laggy. They are working on fixing this issue though. • Server wipes – Right now because of how fast people tend to build random useless buildings in this game the maps can get pretty full. Forcing the mods to wipe the server so that it isn’t crazy laggy. The server I currently play on has to do it about once a week. You don’t lose any of the blueprints you learned but you will be started back naked as a new player when you first log in. • Glitching – This can get pretty annoying. Because it is still an alpha game people tend to find ways to glitch into your base and steal your stuff. It isn’t nearly as bad as it used to be but it can get annoying at times. Conclusion Over all I personally really enjoy this game. I enjoy being able to build anything I can think of and the added risk of being able to die at any time. I would highly recommend if you are going to buy this game to get a friend to buy it at the same time. It makes it a lot easier if you have someone watching your back and helping you gather resources. If you are the type of person who easily gets upset when they have to restart a game or expect everything to be handed to you in a game then I would not recommend it for you.

Second:power cores. In every map, the game is divided in half, with a power generator, a turret, and then the core. Killing the core wins the game, of course. Fully completing everything offered in the game will take a long time, and even after 'finishing' a save file and starting a new one, I still had the same satisfaction going through the game a second time. I have enjoyed countless hours in this game experiencing all that is has to offer, excitedly awaiting the change in seasons and various events in the game, building relationships with the townsfolk, developing my farm and using the money I earn to further develop it as well as expanding my house, fighting my way through the mine--sometimes scrambling to find a ladder to get to the next elevator checkpoint or to the exit when I am low on health and health-replenishing items while running from hordes of enemies--and the feeling of satisfaction as I reached each checkpoint, sometimes getting an item for my efforts. I have not personally played multi-player, so all I can say is that single-player is still a satisfying experience due to the sheer amount of content in the game. This game and its world hold a special place in my heart, there is so much more to this game than what I have mentioned, and it is absolutely worth the cost of buying it to experience all that it has to offer.

The story is pretty much the same so if you'd like the original or you like relatively silly-ish 80's style story's you'll enjoy this one. -The Bad The biggest problem present in the Remake i would argue is the A and B scenario's because there isn't much of a difference between them at all on top of that the feature present in the original that some items are being carried over from A to B isn't there anymore is also a missed opportunity, especially if you consider what could have been done with the more modern mechanics or game engine that the remake works with. another somewhat more minor thing i would argue is that the Free DLC that was added later on is rather lackluster. these issues stated aren't exactly a deal-breaker for me personally but they have to be mentioned. if you are a survival horror game fan this pretty much is a must play if you'd ask me it does the genre and the original game allot of justice despite it's shortcomings.

Spoilers. JC3 is somewhat an upgrade from JC2. Grapple hook + parachute combo is more responsive and it just feels good to fly around. Wingsuit is a good addition but you wont use it much after you figure out how to use grapple + parachute effectively while traveling. Graphics are good but bad at the same time. The sunset, the sky, the sea, explosions. Just beautiful. Game renders stuff from ~10 km away yet it cant render grass or flowers that are 10 meters in front of you. From stable ~100 fps anywhere (settings high, gtx 1070, i5, 16gb ram) to ~40 when theres a lot of explosions. Cars still have shitty driving mechanic. GTA 3 has better driving. AI is horrible. I thought far cry AI is dogshit but this, this is something else. Its impossible to die unless you literally stand still in enemy base so enemy soldiers can kill you but sometimes they still fail. Biggest threats are boats with mounted guns. Helicopters are meh. Due to dogshit AI, sometimes they crash into something random. Maybe it was just bad luck but about half of the time when I tried to hijack enemy helicopters, Rico would grapple awkwardly, hitting helicopter blades which would cause ragdoll effect. Hijacking/"hacking" anything doesnt have QTE like in JC2. There is no HP bar. Its just the same boring system from COD. Taking too much damage? Hide for ~5 seconds to "heal". NO MINIMAP. Every time you wanna check something, you have to open global map.. At least it opens instantly. This time theres no collectable "boxes" for upgrades. You upgrade stuff (cars, helicopters, hook, weapons, etc.) by "Gears". You get "Gears" by doing "feats/challenges". Each "challenge" is related to thing you want to upgrade. For example: to upgrade explosives, you need to find the "challenge". Then you are given a timer and a weapon/vehicle which you have to use to cause as much chaos as possible in given time. You can get 1 to 5 "gears" from one challenge. When you got 5 "gears" then theres no point doing same challenge again - you wont get any more "gears". Cant farm it :(. Its okay change but I still prefer boxes from JC2. Weapons feel okay but there isnt many. Most of the times you will be using rocket launcher/assault rifle. SMGs dont do enough damage and pistols dont have much ammo. Instead of C4 there is some weirdly named explosive that you can plant and then detonate. It never ends, you dont have to refill it/buy it but you can plant only 3 at once (5 is maximum if you upgrade it). Getting an airdrop is free. All you need is a "beacon" (you can collect it from any military base, 5 is maximum). No more cutscenes with sheldon talking shit. You pick whatever you like (weapons/car/boat/plane, etc.), throw beacon wherever you like and then container falls down from the sky. After it hits the ground, all the stuff you ordered just appears in front of you. The world feels smaller because there isnt as many military bases/towns as there is in JC2. Collectibles are quite easy to find. They are marked on you map as "?" when a province has been cleared. And there is a lot less of them too. I dont recommend clearing towns/bases before doing main missions. Its cool they let you do it but then main missions become extremely easy. Everything is cleared, no enemies (apart from the ones a missions spawns) and its just boring. Its better to do the main stuff first and then have some real Just Cause fun. Story mode is shit. Its just there because it has to be there. They tried to be serious about it but it all falls apart from constant cringeworthy stuff Rico or Mario says. Its just so bad. I know this is typical but still: last mission was dogshit. So, Rico, Mario, Annika and Teo travel to a volcano where big bad boss "crashed" his plane or something. He didnt. He is just waiting there in his golden (of course it is golden) helicopter. And.. you fight him. Rico's friends cheer for him I guess? While you have to dodge missiles and shit with your grapple hook. The helicopter has a shield that blocks any damage but it turns itself off for ~4 seconds just for you to attack it. Thats it. Dodge rockets > attack helicopter. ~2 min gg wp, big great boss. At the end there is a cutscene where you can shoot the fuck or let him talk. Either way - he dies. I didnt shoot him; he just jumped into flames himself. GG again. I wasnt expecting much but this is so bad. Maybe he had some hidden base in the volcano. Maybe Rico would have to push through waves of enemies with his friends. No. We have Rico's friends cheering him and the big bad boss telling you to "face him like a man" (literal quote) while sitting in a fkin golden helicopter. What?????? GG WP Overall its better than JC2 and DEFINETLY better than JC4. Besides - I got this game for ~£1.90 while it was on a sale so got my moneys worth. GG WP GOLDEN HELICOPTER BIG BOSS DICTATOR MAN, GG WP. Btw. Annika is bae.

[b][u]Stealth is literally broken[/u][/b] Guards have an aura of awareness instead of a cone of vision like many stealth games. This aura is affected by your level of threat which is based on your weapon loadout and body armor which affects how fast you will be "made" if spotted. The problem is this aura is 360 degrees around the guard. Like a spider-sense. So even if a guard doesn't see you, you can still be spotted if you remain within his aura for too long. Guard pathing is horrible. They just wander around aimlessly, will stare at walls, clip into one another so you'll have two guards literally on top of eachother, and walk over the top of solid objects or clip through them. [b][u]Lack of heist information[/u][/b] Most levels you don't need it. Find/drill the safe, smash the case/grab the loot, etc. The more eclectic missions like Shadow Raid, Framing Frame, or Rats you have very specific rules. Rules that are terribly conveyed or not conveyed at all in your mission briefing or by Bain. In your first time playing Shadow Raid you are stealing a wide array of items. Cocaine, guns, money, paintings, but never does the game actually tell you what these items look like, what the containers that could hold them look like, or even that these are the items you're stealing. The same with the final mission of Framing Frame. 5 electronic items needed and you have no idea what they look like. Sometimes they appear on your map with gold auras, but sometimes they don't. I don't know if this is by design or if it's just terrible design. Having looked at Overkill's track record I'd go with the latter. I mean come on! You see those stupid photos during the planning phase of gage courier items and the type of cops you'll see. How about instead you include a few pictures of my freaking mission objectives? [b][u]Syncing issues are still here.[/u][/b] Player 1: "I just killed a guard behind a wall and am answering his pager." Player 2: "Really? Cause on my screen he's in front of a doorway right in front of a camera." Player 1: "Soooo is he behind the wall or under the camera?" Alarm sounds... Player 1: q_q So syncing in PD2 is still trash but don't worry I'm sure Overkill will get to it after they've released their 20th mission DLC. Or maybe in PD3. Whichever comes first. [b][u]The game is either boring or frustrating[/u][/b] [u]Boring[/u] For low level players bank missions and armored transports are a waste of time. Go bank, or the bank heist: you drill the safe/wait for the timer. After waiting between 3 or 4 minutes you're greeted by walls of lock boxes each one taking 45 secs to pick. Multiply that by 30 or 40 boxes and you can see what I'm talking about. The Enforcer Saw, which can open lockboxes in 1 second is a very high tier item. So you have to play the game a TON before you can play the game AND have fun. O_o In fact many missions you stealth will require you to sit around waiting for something to open or mom to come get you. In the Night Club after killing all the guards, subduing all hostages and disabling all cameras; I had to wait for the drill to open the door to the office. Wait while drilling the safe and then wait 4 more minutes for the get away driver. That's not including time added when I had to reset the drills. Keep in mind this is happening in a level that I've now made impossible for the cops to show. There seriously needs to be some method of speeding things up when in situations where you've perfectly stealthed the level. [u]Frustrating[/u] A lot of the difficulty in the game is due to bad design. When dozers can snipe you through a window on the 2nd floor of a meth house, from across the street. Cops being able to shoot grenades out of mid-air having them explode in your face, yet there is nothing the player can do to combat smoke or flash bangs. If I can't interfere with their thrown utility weapons, they shouldn't be able to interfere with mine. Snipers that are so far away you need a sniper rifle (a DLC item) to hit them with any consistency. Unbelievably stupid placement of mission assets. My favorite is during the train heist, the 2nd thermal drill is dropped into a ravine surrounded by police. Trying to answer multiple pagers if you're unlucky enough to have two guards die on top of eachother. Levels that feel like they were designed by crazy people. Having to wait for Bain to tell you how to make meth. Watching the pilot miss the cage 3 times despite purchasing the "ace pilot" asset. During Go Bank, me and my crew wasted all our zip ties subduing all civs on the street and in the bank. Then I watched as 5 - 8 civs randomly spawned in all at once just before the vault opened. No patrol path, they just walked single file into the bank and piled up by the counter turning a perfectly civil robbery into a bloodbath. This game has sucked for a good while before microtransations were implemented.

Cuphead is 1930s cartoons stylized boss battles platformer. You take control over the titular character (and if you have friends, like I don't, you can play local coop mode with your buddy Mugman) and you try to defeat a bunch of bosses, because you need their stuff :P Now, I was waiting for this game for years, I was afraid that it might end up being poopy like some other games in the past with infinitely long development process (cough cough, Duke Nukem Forever, No Man's Sky...), but I'm happy to report that Cuphead is just awesome! Everything is great about it. Crazy, hand drawn (!) animations, beautiful soundtrack, hilarious cartoonish sound effects, fluent controls, insane multistaged bosses with the most over the top goofy attacks, upgrades to your loadout, special powerful attacks, dash/parry system and so on and so forth :P The difficulty is high and you can adjust it before starting each boss battle. It's based on patterns recognition and your reflexes, this way you rarely feel like you've been screwed by RNG. You're going to die. A lot. But I just can't get mad at this game for killing me mercilessly when everything is so cheerful, colorful and cute :P It definetely has 'just one more try' syndrome and it's great. You want to kick the enemy's butt and when you do you feel amazing! And then you go to the next beautifully animated boss battle and you get the crap kicked out of you again, the cycle never ends and you're happy to be a part of this pandemonium :) So Cuphead. Unique, super fun game! I highly recommend checking it out! 9/10

Okay, so here's my updated review for one of my most treasured games yet. Me and Terraria go way back, not as back as others, but quite far back. All the way to 2013 when I first got steam, this was my second purchase ((I'm pretty sure)), and I do have to say, Terraria has come a very long way from where it once was in 2013, and even a few years before that. The reason why I adore this game so much is because of the updates and replay-ability with each one. With each new FREE update, it feels like I'm playing the game like I just bought it yesterday. Here are some Pros and Cons about Terraria too: Pros: +Nearly unlimited replay value, ranging from items and different classes for your character to be with armour sets. +Still being Updated by the developers, and keeping the same price through each update as well. +Multiplayer, although a bit laggy at times with steam friend servers, it's quite decent compared to other games, where server hosting takes too much time and hassel in most peoples eyes. ~This might not be a pro for most, or a con either, but your character upgrades and becomes better with what you do and what items you collect or want to focus on. Your character has no EXP system, and isn't needed. HP and Mana are increased through collecting items ((Heart Crystals and Mana Stars)). And buffs are mostly made from potions, and also collected from loot, or fishing. Some people might hate this type of gameplay, but I find it interesting and its what gives Terraria its style. Cons: -Sometimes a little bit too Grindy. Nearing the end of the game, when you enter a more dangerous version of the game, also known as "Hardmode" things seem to slow down slightly. You have to kill more enemies to get souls, which are used to make the new Hardmode bosses. It get's slightly annoying, sitting there and waiting for souls of light/night to drop when you're trying to get better gear or fight better and harder bosses. -Steam Server Connections. Like I said before in the pros section, the servers do tend to become slightly laggy, and frozen when playing with friends. I don't know if that's our New Zealand internet being stupid, or if it's the Steam Server hosting. Anyway, it's slightly annoying, but not too bad once you get use to it. Still a con though. In conclusion?: If you feel like you'd enjoy a game where there is ever expanding enemies, items, armours, and events, then i'd Highly suggest Terraria. With me clocking in nearly 400 Hours (Probably 400+ in a few days), I highly suggest trying this game out. For what it's worth, it's definetly worth paying for full price. P.S: There's also modding support with external mod loaders. Just in case you wanted to know ;3 TLDR: Buy the game, try it out. If a constantly updated and ever expanding game isn't your type of Coffee, then at least you helped the devs continue this amazing project <3

I was recommended this game because I'm a big fan of the Phoenix Wright series and I was told that it had a lot of similarities. Like Phoenix Wright, it's a visual novel of sorts, so most of the game involves reading through lots of dialogue and using your brain to solve mysteries. However, this game has a bit more in terms of minigames that you need to complete to solve the puzzles. Phoenix Wright has some, yes, but only occasionally. Fortunately, if you have trouble with these there are different difficulties you can choose, and you can also engage in "dating sim" activities in order to unlock skills that will help you. As far as the story goes, this one is a bit more plot-centric than Phoenix Wright, while the latter focuses more on the characters. It's not that the characters in Danganronpa are uninteresting, but they do tend to follow stereotypes a bit more often. There were still some that I liked quite a bit and I was not disappointed by the overall story even though I was able to figure out parts of it fairly easily. As for the puzzles themselves, I didn't think they were as tricky as the ones in the original Phoenix Wright trilogy for sure. It was pretty easy for me to figure out what I needed to deduce. However, the game makes you work for it more through the minigames and that adds an extra level of challenge. I enjoyed going through all of the chapters. In addition, the music is excellent and there are a number of catchy tunes that are worth adding to your video game music playlist. I also enjoyed the art style quite a bit, and thought that the atmosphere was creepy. The game has some extra value, too, in the form of School Mode, which gives you some more "dating sim" activities to do though this part isn't necessary to complete for the story. It does, however, make it easy to unlock all of the skills that you can use in more difficult playthroughs. My only real complaint is that you have to do a lot of traveling back and forth to the various characters, and this gets more tedious as the game progresses because you have fewer people to talk to. The second game no longer has this problem so it looks like other people had the same complaint. Anyway, if you really loved the Phoenix Wright series, you will also enjoy this one and I can't wait to see where this story goes as I am currently working on the second game.

TL;DR AT BOTTOM Original Review (11/21/2018 Amazing, an absolute improvement upon HITMAN (2016), more weapons, gameplay elements, missions, etc. Sean bean is proud to be the first Elusive Target, I can see why. ______________________________________________________________ Revised Review (07/23/2020 After almost 2 years of playing HITMAN 2, I am excited for the third installment in the reboot trilogy. I have finished all the missions, bonus missions, challenges, official escalations, Sniper Assassin challenges, Ghost Mode challenges and all achievements with over 400 hours under my belt at level 750+, so I have lots of game experience to work with. Gonna say, it's probably a 9.8/10 hands down, very little they would need to change in order to make it a perfect HITMAN game in my books. It's really damn good, the game feels like an absolute treat to play. The gameplay is very fluid and changes really well based on your actions, and the AI is smart enough to be challenging for new and experienced players, but also dumb enough for it to feel fun for all skill types, and even comedic at times from the AI dialogue, a nice touch. The content of this game is nothing short of abundant, albeit, a good 60-70%% of the unlocks are unused by me personally, just because there are unlocks to focus on getting that make the best possible experience of play, and I'll go over just a few. The 'Krugermier 2-2' is the best (stealth) pistol in the game and should be unlocked ASAP by any player looking to play through HITMAN 2 more than a few times, or to replay for content being the only sub-sonic pistol in the game (so you can shoot it within like "tip-touching" distance of people and they wont hear it, unlike any other pistol), as well as having 10 round magazines, compared to the base 7 from the starting pistol. The only drawback of the pistol is accuracy, I'd probably gauge it's 50% more inaccurate compared to the stock ICA pistol, but really it isn't a problem for this game, you're not gonna be shooting anybody from very long distances with it, and speaking of shooting at long ranges... The 'Seiger 300 Ghost' is hands-down the best sniper rifle in the game (and should also be unlocked ASAP), this is just about unanimously agreed upon by anybody who has unlocked it. It is the only 4X zoom sniper, with a fair amount of ammunition, pretty steady to aim, with snow-mo bullet time, easy to aim/handle, and is also sub-sonic for use good use near NPCs. The 'ICA Electrocution Phone' as one of the best tools to unlock, as it is a near fail proof way of getting easy Silent Assassin kills, as the target killed by it counts as an accident kill, and will not void your Silent Assassin rating. It can be used as a audible distraction (thrown) and can lure NPCs as well as they will go over to pick it up when seen. This is the singular item that Elusive Target missions revolve around now, as it is easy for them to be killed with little risk. The Briefcase, of any kind, it is a very powerful tool, with multiple functions of distraction, enforcer removal (via. re-locating the briefcase to a gun-container), pacification tool, and a smuggling tool. The 'Seiger 300 Ghost' can instantly be taken in and out of the briefcase, with no animation, further enhancing the "Best Sniper" in the entire game. -End Of Weapon Discussion- All I can really say to change gameplay wise it just to make the AI slightly smarter when looking around for you (like peeking around corners). Also, having enforcers that look for you have a chance to search nearby containers/closets/cabinets you can hide in but scale based on difficulty, such as 0-5% for 'Casual', 10-15% for 'Professional', and 25-50% for 'Master', but anything like that would be cool to see, it would give an extra degree of "oh crap" when you mess up stealth plays in a mission. What I will ask to change GAME-WISE would be to NOT make elusive targets 1 time FOREVER gone, as it is really annoying to blow up or electrocute yourself in preparing for a 1-time assassination contract. It's the only thing that pisses me off genuinely. If they had a system to try it again, like a 3 or 5 multi-stage escalation that you kill the Elusive Target at the end of it, but if you die right at the very end, you start from stage one, I WOULD BE FINE WITH THAT! Then I could actually try it again, and just waste my time doing the previous stages for like an hour or two before getting to kill the target, but getting only like a week to do the target would probably be a tad short, maybe like 10-14 days would be better for an idea like that. At the very least, just don't flunk my mission attempt if I kill myself in the mission by my own means. Also the Lockpick and electronic keycard hacers are very good too. The one gripe I have is how useless like 80% if the unlocks are compared to all the other unlocks in the same category as some of them, as one usually stands higher than all of the other unlocks. Suits are also pretty cool, wish there were even more, even if there are already too many to choose from hahaha. ______________________________________________________________ TL;DR This game is very, very good, a 9.8/10 IMO, with very good gameplay elements, story, and content. Get the 'Krugermier 2-2', 'Seiger 300 Ghost', and 'ICA Electrocution Phone' if you want to play more seriously or long-term. Use and abuse the Briefcase (especially with the 'Seiger 300 Ghost'). Elusive Targets are very good, but the way they designed are pretty bad. This game is worth buying with all the content included, no questions asked, it will keep you busy for a good month or two if you play to get everything.

When I bought this for 1 dollar suring a summer sale, I never thought it would be so enjoyable. I bought it with a friend and started playing it and discovered how much content it had -- it's almost overwhelming. There is so much to do, that in my only playthrough (played it for more than 80 hours) I still haven't done everything you can. I will divide this review into different aspects of the game, as follows: [u] Gameplay [/u] 10/10 Pretty simple and easy to learn, but can get a bit more complex through classes later as the playthrough develops. There are a lot of ways to play the game thanks to the classes, which instead of depending directly on your character, depend on your items. Because of the wide variety of them, there are millions of combinations to fit your style, and in case you want to switch, you won't have to start a whole new character. [u] Crafting [/u] 10/10 Leaving aside the huge amount of items you can find by exploring caves and defeating enemies, there is even a longer list of craftable items, making it almost impossible that you'll ever have one of each. Crafting is demanding though, and most of the game you'll spend your time consulting wiki's to see where you can find the certain material you need to craft the item you want. It is overall a very rewarding experience and it feels like it's worth your time; one of the most satisfying moments of the game is not defeating a boss, but getting the sword you've been wanting to craft for so long (well, at least imo). [u] Building [/u] 8/10 Building does take an important role in the game, unlike minecraft and other survival games, where it is more of a luxury. In Terraria, when you build a house, an NPC will come to live in it. All of these NPC's offer a service, usually selling particular sorts of items or giving you buffs when near them. Even though the rules for housing are pretty simple, nothing stops you to build huge mansions, castles, or whatever you want, so if you're feeling creative there's pretty much unlimited possibilites of thing you can build (there is an enourmous variety of blocks: different kinds of wood, blocks, stones, bricks, metal, etc...) [u] Combat [/u] 9/10 Combat may not always feel balanced, and during certain parts of the game it may get tough, especially when switching to hardmode (it's like the second half of a playthrough). The concept is pretty simple though, the deeper you go in caves, the harder it gets. The whole point of the first part of the game is getting to hell (lowest part of the world) and defeating a boss, so you WILL need to get better items, either by crafting or by finding them. Once you get the hang of it, you'll understand certain fights are imposible without an upgrade. [u] Multiplayer [/u] 10/10 Now this is what made me love this game so much, I probably wouldn't even had finished the game if it weren't for this feature. The game has a lot to offer, and a lot of challenges, and playing it with a friend makes it even better (well, it does happen with every multiplayer game). It sort of becomes an epic adventure for your posse. If you're planning to buy the game, but have no friends that have it, I would definetely recommend buying an extra copy for one of your friends.(that's actually what I did) [u] Overall [/u] 9.5/10 I usually get bored of a game after the initial 5 hours... thisi is not the case. There is always one more thing to do, one more boss to defeat, one more item to get. Once you achieve your current goal, there is always one waiting right there for you. Most of the times you don't even know it, and that makes it even more enjoyable for some reason. It was great to finally kill the boss you've been trying so hard to, just to go to the wiki and look for whatever you should do next. Also, the game gets constantly updated with tons of new content, so it probably won't get old soon. Must buy.

Its a must play.After a few years of not-so-great games, a polished gem was created. After so many hours spent with almost no rest, i got the ending. Then i figured out that was just one of them.One of 26 to be exact.Which makes me think, what more could be done? I`ll try to keep this review spoiler free, and as short as I can, but there is just too much to to cover. Lets split it into 4 categories: General, Pros, Cons, and Overall. 1.General. Not much games can make you go over 6+ hours with no breaks. This is an exception. Beautifull open world, that seems grim at first, but warms you afterwards. The map itself is not very large, but big enough to make you come back to areas over and over to see what you have missed. Combat is flawless. Not even a single bug was found , and to be honest, its a large variety of weapons and combos. Camera movement keeps switching from area to area, making new and interesting ways to play.Its 2D, now 3D, now arcade etc. There are so many ways to play, that I can`t even cover them all here. Story is really good. Like REALLY GOOD. S.E. made a masterpiece. (a few unnecessery moments overall, but understandable). Characters...well there are more different characters here then i can name in any other games.But they all seem so close together (not gonna spoil this part, you gotta see for yourself) Animations are done almost perfectly. The slow-walking mimicing the moving of a top model (2B and A2), and goofy movement for 9S. Over 10 charaters you are gonna play as, so its not gonna bore you soon (Note: i needed 30h to get one final ending. Just one.) 2.Pros. +Atmosphere is done amazingly. For a post-apocaliptic game, everything is so dark and heavy to look at, until you find the soft spots (not gonna spoil again) +Characters feel unique, refreshing.Only a few stereotypes. +Varity of gameplay-styles.A LOT of weapons and abilites you can use. So many combos to do, and so much to try out. +Storyrich. Makes you question almost everything about life itself. Very philosophical. (can`t go into detail without spoiling anything) +Quests and sidequests are actually, fun. No stupid ones like:follow me here, and protect me there etc.Also, some quest have a brand new and deep story for themselves.Don`t skip a single sidequest. +Much, much more, but most of them are spoilers, sorry :/ 3.Cons. -Saves. You can only save your progress on the Terminals, and over a close areas around them.Also, some missions can not be saved until they are over, so buckle up for at least 45min to some of them, where you can`t save in between. -DLC. The outfits you get via DLC can only be aquired after you clear lvl 80 arenas x3 times.At the moment of finishing first game, im lvl 57. So don`t expect lvl 1 skins.You are gonna work had for them. -Some Terminals (save spots) do not have fast-travel, so good luck walking over to them again if you forgot something. -What is the point of fishing? Yes, you can fish to get some small amouts of money, but i saw no purpose for it. -There was no need for a `secret` blacksmith. -A2 has no Lightattack combo (If you hold the light-attack button with A2, you just Taunt.Kinda usless if you ask me) -Minor sidequest annoyance (muliple travels for no reason, but only a few) 4.Overall. Story: 9/10 (Spoilers) Charaters: 9/10 (Spoilers) World: 8/10 (a bit more variety would have been nice- talking about animals and robot types) Music: 8/10 (it can get repetitive, but still very nice) Main Quests: 9/10 (Spoilers) Side Quests: 7/10 (because of that multiple go forth-back bs) Lenght: 9/10 (makes you come back) Overall feeling: 9.5/10 A game to never forget. Top 3 games of all time for me. Will come back to it.I do hope a sequel will come. So, final answers: Is it worth to buy? - Yes. Even for a full price.(only 3 recorded sales within a year) Is it worth the time? -Yes. Feels a bit empty after you finish it. Which is always good. Is the DLC worth it? - Depends. If you want to play just for the story, don`t buy it. If you want to gett al the achievements and stuff, do get it. P.S. There are a lot of forum treads to help you out if you get stuck. There is even a *HELP* bot in the main terminal area, which can help you get started on the basics.

This game is an all immersive survival battle royale vs. man vs. wild (if you roll on a pvp server). The content and map size is great. Big enough to get lost in and always more to see and do. There is a huge grind element, but I thoroughly enjoy it and there is great satisfaction to be had with the crafting and building of bases and armour/weapons. You get to test and try your own imagination and if you can dream it up, then you can almost always build it (providing it fits within the laws of physics). Taming can be a drag if it really isn't your thing, but again I enjoy the hunt and defence of the unconscious tame once you do manage to tranq it out. I thoroughly recommend using spikes to keep out sneaky players who might try and steal your narcotics and food source, and this prevents dilos and raptors etc. from coming up and snacking on your prospective dino tame as well. I won't sugar coat it... if you play on a pvpve server. You will die at some point, you will lose dinos at some point and you will get raided at some point... but hey that is what makes it great... Tears will be shed at times (figuratively speaking) and while it rips you a new one to log in and see a new scenic window to your base where a metal wall use to be, you will find great satisfaction and immense pleasure in returning the favour to those who have wronged you, or the nearest chump who just looked at you the wrong way. Remember that this beast of a game is still in early access, but it is fully playable and extremely enjoyable... hence my racked up hours against it. The developers have done extremely well and are always one upping themselves as they add more content and optimize the game as it progresses towards its official release date. KEEP UP THE GOOD WORK STUDIO WILDCARD!!! These guys keep adding patches and updates several times a week and the release of new content and hints of upcoming stuff keeps you interested. If you don't mind a good grind session, you love dinos or even just pvp and ruining someone else's day or if you just like to express your artistic flare with your base design then this game has something for you. Despite it combines a few elements from other genres Hunt Showdown managed to mix them together and create a truly unique experience. If you look at it superficial it could be a match-based survival game or maybe a battle royale and it is of course both of that but also more. The games goal is to track a monster by collecting clues, kill said monster, banish it and extract with a bounty token to get money. Then you can buy better weapons and traits and repeat the process. While in a match there are far more dangers than just the boss, the map is littered with round about 8 to 10 different kinds of monsters you all need to learn how to get rid of quickly and possibly noiselessly because the are up to 12 players per match who will more often than not try to kill you to get the bounty for themselves. If you lose your Hunter he’s gone and all equipment he carried with him which means you need to buy yourself a new one. This creates a tension barely any game can keep up with. I for one only had similar experiences with Eve Online which has also a permadeath feature. Also very well done is the sound in this game. It’s binaural which means you can pinpoint exactly where each sound is coming from and this adds a lot to the experience and creates even more tension. After a while you learn how the guns sound from a distance, where the shots are coming from and how to effectively track other hunters by the sound they make. If you want a high risk, high reward game with a lot of tension, very good sound and interesting weapons then Hunt maybe the right game for you.

I played the game through to the end, and did most of the optional zones, missions, and unlocks. Overall its a good game, very few bugs, turn based strategy akin to XCOM series (honestly its pretty much a reskin). The characters are unique which makes them sort of cool, and there is some decent humor and voice-acting. The reason I give it thumbs down is for two reasons: miniscule campaign length and lack of replayability. XCOM can last hundreds of hours, and each time you play your heroes and tactics all change, you try this combination of squaddies or that, you try out psychic abilities on another playthrough, you download some DLC or even steam community content (e.g. XCOM Long War series which was outstanding). Mutant YZ is like a tunnel vision version of XCOM, with a narrow, linear campaign and five set soldiers which you cannot modify or customize at all, really. Its like playing XCOM with five soldiers, one from each class, with set skill trees. The campaign itself was suuuuuper short IMO, and very, very obivous how it would end, no unexpected plot twists, etc. Plus to that the ending was sort of left in the air. It was akin to ending the Star Wars franchise with Empire Strikes Back and never getting Return of the Jedi. Summary: If you like XCOM and strategy games with an occasional joke about 'ancient technology', and you can get this on sale, its probably worth it. If any of the above conditions do not apply, skip it.

It's time for me to write a review as well, having played through the game and basically seen every bit of content it offers, without the special event monsters (yet). So, going forward to it: The story: It's a fun one, fitting for the Monster Hunter series, and while definitely not the main reason to play the game (we want to battle against oversized monsters after all!) it's immersive. Definitely worth playing through, watching all the cutscenes and listening to what people say, without it, the game would only be half as good. It does a good job in setting up the world, as well as keeping it 'reasonable' as to why everything is as it is. At least in the sense of the Monster Hunter universe. Solo Gameplay: It's fun, and the whole game is able to be done alone, no more unobtainable 'high-rank rewards' which one can't get without other players, and therefore after shutting off the servers sooner or later. It's actually the first game in the Monster Hunter series (for me) which I've seen this, and it's a very very good choice, making it reasonable to get back to it while also not feeling awful since all the nicely presented upgrades are simply unavailable. The Monsters feel overwhelming as it should be, and while the start is fairly easy, the further the game progresses the more skill is needed, giving a nice incentive to actually get better. Without being punished for failing (besides the used items) it's also not frustrating to fail. There is nothing excruciating on the line, but there is always a reward ahead. Multiplayer: I had 3 disconnects throughout the whole playthrough of the game, 2 happened because of my own fault, so a single actually real disconnect which put me into the place of having to fight solo again with a bad layout for doing so. Well, it happens, and it was the absolute exception. Besides that, the gameplay in a group is solid, a well versed troop can take down everything in a short time and it definitely makes the game easier, materials are obtained quicker but the money reward is split between everyone, so it balances out in a good way. Synchronization hiccups are rare, and unless you're fairly unlucky to both have one AND be in the wrong spot you might get hit by a monster which changes their position. Throughout the whole playthrough this hasn't happened to me, synchronization errors though have popped up a whooping amount of... 4 times in 70 hours of playtime, for several short seconds. So, solid as well. All in all, another good experience. Ease of life changes over former Monster Hunter games: You can actually see the whole weapon trees, which is fantastic. You can store unlimited amounts of armor and weapons, as well as see which ones you already own, also fantastic. Effects of jewels are described, which baffled me in the former titles as to why that hadn't been the case. The effects of food buffs is listed. And many more I can't recall right now. Things which could've been done better: While the food buffs are listed, their effects are sadly not, leaving you to look it up in a guide respectively, or simply choosing them blind. The amount of different creatures to hunt is a bit lacking compared to some other instances of the game, the nintendo switch version of Monster Hunter has over 100 creatures, here it's not even that amount with the small and 'endemic' creatures put into account. Fishing is fairly useless, it played a nice side-role in other parts, but in World they are neglected, leaving a nice opportunity for a bit of relaxing fun during explorations out. Jumping onto monsters is unintuitive, when does it happen? Is it based on luck? Some specific situations or positions you need to hit the monster? It's unclear, and never properly explained, hence why it's not used that often without specific weapons. All in all, I give the game a rating of 9/10, Capcom did a good job on making their franchise better, it feels like a proper whole game and even after finishing the main quest there is still a lot of collecting items and hunting to be done. Weren't it for the few tidbits that could've been remedied easily it would get a 10/10.

Es ist mal wieder Survival-Time. Holz und Steine sind gesammelt, die erste rudimentäre Axt und eine Steinspitzhacke sind auch im Inventar. Bogen und Pfeile… check. Bauplan craften, vier Wände und ein Dach, Schlafsack, Schmelzofen, Werkbank… läuft doch prima. Bis auf einmal nachts Schritte zu hören sind. Da ist einer vor unserer Hütte. Klick. Und unsere Tür steht in Flammen. Da will uns doch tatsächlich einer mit dem Flammenwerfer heimsuchen -.- Jetzt schlau sein und warten. Die Tür ist weg, die Flammen auch… und schnell rennen wir raus in die Nacht. Geschafft! Sicherheitshalber warten wir noch zehn Minuten, bis er auch sicher nicht mehr da ist, bevor wir zu unserer Hütte zurückgehen und nachgucken, was von unserem Loot noch in den Kisten ist *Schock* Der Kerl hat uns nicht nur alles geklaut, was wir haben, er hat auch noch eine neue Tür eingesetzt und ein Schloss drangehängt. Das war es mit unserer Base… Mit Stock und Stein kommen wir da nicht mehr rein. Jetzt gibt es nur zwei Möglichkeiten: Rust deinstallieren oder es so oft neu probieren, bis wir selber der Mistkerl sind, der anderen die Hütte „raidet“. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1370833249 Rust erschien 2013 hier auf Steam und blieb fast fünf Jahre im Early Access, bis es im Februar 2018 endlich offiziell released wurde. Ich verrate euch jetzt, warum Rust – meiner Meinung nach – eigentlich ein gutes Spiel ist, aber worauf ihr euch da einlasst. Gameplay Wie schon eingangs beschrieben, ist Rust ein klassisches Survival-Action-Adventure im Stil von DayZ, Ark, 7 Days to Die und wie sie alle heißen. In der Ego-Perspektive steuert ihr euren zunächst nackten Recken durch eine offene Spielwelt, sammelt Holz und Steine, baut euch eine Basis, sammelt Waffen (vom Bogen bis zum Raketenwerfer ist alles dabei) und kämpft PvE und PvP ums Überleben. Und genau im letzten Punkt liegt der Hund begraben. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1372199356 PvE bedeutet im Prinzip nur, dass in der Spielwelt – meistens in der Nähe des besten Loots – ein paar blau gekleidete Forscher rumlaufen, die mit Maschinengewehren auf euch schießen, wenn ihr ihnen zu nahe kommt. Die sind aber nach ein paar Spielstunden keine ernstzunehmende Bedrohung mehr für euch. Anders verhält sich das jedoch in Sachen PvP. Ich habe selten so aggressive und unfreundliche (menschliche) Spieler in einem Spiel gesehen, wie in Rust. Selbst wenn man nackt ist (also klar erkennbar keinen wertvollen Loot besitzt) wird man „grundlos“ umgeschossen und selbst Anfängerhütten mit Holzwänden werden rücksichtslos geraidet. Jetzt könnte man auf die Idee kommen, den Spielern einen Vorwurf zu machen… und manchmal mag das bestimmt auch berechtigt sein. Aber genau das ist eben der Sinn dieses Spiels. Es gibt keine erlesenen Basis-Bau-Rezepte. Es gibt keinen nennenswerten Endgame-Content. Der einzige Sinn des Spiels ist das Aufleveln der Werkbank um so zunächst einfache Pistolen über Sturmgewehre bin hin zum Sprengstoff zu erforschen und craften zu können, damit man damit dann auf die Jagd nach anderen Spielern und deren Behausungen gehen kann. Die Starken jagen die Schwachen. So funktioniert Rust nun einmal. Und wer meint, „casual“ auf einem der Server unterwegs sein zu können und jeden Tag „ein Stündchen“ vor sich hin zu spielen, der sei gewarnt. Wer so spielt, gehört in Rust definitiv zu den Schwachen. Grafik Rust sieht einfach super aus. Die Entwickler von Facepunch Studios zaubern mit der Unity-Engine ein inzwischen optisch tadelloses Spiel auf die Bildschirme. Schönere Sonnenauf- bzw. -untergänge mit ihrem orange bis lilafarbenem Licht habe ich selten gesehen. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1371422484 Die Optik fordert jedoch auch ihren Tribut. Bei Mittelklasserechnern mit vollen Einstellungen gehen die FPS gerne mal in den Keller. Ich empfehle in diesem Fall, das Gras etwas zu reduzieren, was zugleich auch der besseren Übersicht im Spiel zugutekommt. Umfang Rust bietet euch im Hauptmenü eine Vielzahl von unterschiedlichen Servern, auf denen ihr (jedes Mal beginnend bei null) ins Abenteuer starten könnt. Klassischerweise wählt ihr einen „offiziellen Server“ und spielt dort den klassischen Spielmodus, also Survival, gegen alle auf dem Server befindlichen anderen menschlichen Spieler. Der Servername gibt euch dabei Aufschluss über Land (und somit Sprache) des Servers und über den Spielmodus. Regelmäßig sind auch Zusätze, wie „beginner friendly“ oder „noob friendly“ zu finden, was zu Beginn vielleicht nicht schlecht ist ;-) Neben den offiziellen Servern gibt es noch „Community-Server“, welche von Spielern betrieben werden sowie „modded Server“ auf denen sich eine Vielzahl von anderen Spielmodi und Spielvarianten finden. Wie und wo man da selbst richtig aufgehoben ist, muss jeder selber entscheiden. Es gibt die verschiedensten Spielvarianten von Deathmatch (mit sofortigem bewaffneten Respawn) bis hin zu superfreundlichen Servern ohne PvE und PvP, wo man einfach nur in Ruhe vor sich hin bauen kann. Rust bietet also zwar durchaus Abwechslung in den Spielmodi, der tatsächlich klassische Modus und somit auch die Server, die am besten besucht sind, sind aber klar die offiziellen mit dem oben beschriebenen Standardmodus von Rust. Cheater-Problem? Man kann nicht „Rust“ sagen, ohne das gleich jemand bereit steht und etwas zum Thema „Cheater“ berichtet und tatsächlich scheint Rust zu Beginn stark von diesem Problem heimgesucht worden zu sein. Ich hatte jedoch in den nun beinahe 100 Stunden, in denen ich Rust gespielt habe, nie das Gefühl, gerade von einem Hacker getötet worden zu sein. Ich schätze, dass die, die mich gekillt und geraidet haben, einfach nur besser waren, als ich ;-) Errungenschaften Gute Nachrichten für alle Achievement-Sammler. Rust beinhaltet 48 Errungenschaften, die alle lediglich an das Bestehen des Tutorials geknüpft sind. Man muss keinen Gegner töten und kein Haus raiden, aber dennoch ein Weilchen spielen. Diese Errungenschaften sollten für niemanden wirklich eine große Herausforderung darstellen. Da sie sich aber nur auf offiziellen Servern freischalten lassen, muss man sich schon – zumindest zeitweise für die Achievements – den echten Spielern unter den echten harten Spielbedingungen stellen. Fazit Rust ist grundsätzlich ein gutes Spiel. Es hat ein zielstrebiges Konzept, eine sehr schöne Optik, eine aktive Community und knallharte Emotionen zu bieten, verlangt dafür aber Taktik, gewisse Skills an der Waffe und wirklich viel Zeit um die ersten Stunden und Tage eines „frischen Servers“ mitzunehmen, wo dort noch keine Spieler mit Raketenwerfer und C4 unterwegs sind (also nur im Urlaub/ in den Ferien spielen^^). Wer kein Problem damit hat, nach stundenlangem Spielen alles zu verlieren und wieder von vorne anzufangen und auch mit knallharten und erbarmungslosen menschlichen Spielern umgehen kann, ohne die Maus an die Wand zu feuern oder in Depressionen zu verfallen, der kann in Rust viele unterhaltsame Stunden verbringen. Für Casual-Gamer und Pazifisten ist Rust hingegen absolut nichts. Die aktuellen 31,99 Euro hier auf Steam halte ich – in Anbetracht des Alters des Spiels – für etwas zu teuer. In den häufigen Sales ist Rust aber regelmäßig für unter 20 Euro zu haben. Von mir gibt es eine Kaufempfehlung aber mit ganz klaren Einschränkungen!
